title: Balanced derived scalar comparisons of finite Tate lines commute with pullback
statement:
Let $N\geq1$ be invertible on a scheme $T$ and let $f:T'\to T$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a unital map of finite commutative rings with $NA=NB=0$. For $V=T,T'$ work in the ordinary unbounded derived categories $D(V_{\mathrm{et}},R)$ of constant-ring module sheaves, $R=A,B$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], and set $E_V=-\otimes^L_{A_V}B_V$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Regard sheaves as degree-zero complexes. Put $R_V(1)=\mu_{N,V}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/N)_V}R_V$, where $\mu_{N,V}(U)=\{z\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)^\times:z^N=1\}$ and residue classes act by powers [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line].

The ordinary balanced maps
$$a\otimes b\longmapsto\varphi(a)b,\qquad (z\otimes a)\otimes b\longmapsto z\otimes\varphi(a)b$$
induce specified isomorphisms $\theta^0_V:E_V(A_V)\xrightarrow\sim B_V$ and $\theta^1_V:E_V(A_V(1))\xrightarrow\sim B_V(1)$ in these derived categories. Their ordinary inverses are $b\mapsto1\otimes b$ and $z\otimes b\mapsto(z\otimes1)\otimes b$. These are the comparisons obtained by deriving ordinary coefficient extension on the degree-zero sheaves. Their shifts and finite direct sums are the canonical exact additive-functor comparisons, preserving the summand inclusions and projections.

Write $u_R:f_R^*R_T(1)\xrightarrow\sim R_{T'}(1)$ for the roots-induced inverse-image identification [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] and $\lambda_M:f_B^*E_TM\xrightarrow\sim E_{T'}f_A^*M$ for the canonical derived tensor/pullback comparison [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons]. Then the following equality of actual derived morphisms holds, and also holds after any common shift:
$$\theta^1_{T'}\circ E_{T'}(u_A)\circ\lambda_{A_T(1)}=u_B\circ f_B^*(\theta^1_T).$$
Likewise, writing $e_R:f_R^*R_T\xrightarrow\sim R_{T'}$ for the canonical unit comparison of inverse image [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons], $$\theta^0_{T'}\circ E_{T'}(e_A)\circ\lambda_{A_T}=e_B\circ f_B^*(\theta^0_T),$$ also after any common shift. No flatness of $B$ over $A$ is assumed.

source.place: Charts: 'free rank-one summands, whose derived extension is the ordinary one'; normalized twist identifications used in retained splitting Steps 1 and 4

proof.text: For $V=T,T'$ and $R=A,B$, the finite-twist-line lemma applies: $N$ is invertible on $T'$ because units remain units under a scheme morphism, and $NR=0$. Thus $R_V$ and $R_V(1)$ are flat. Their degree-zero complexes are bounded above and K-flat by the K-flat closure lemma. Apply the change-of-rings computation to the identity resolutions of $A_V[0]$ and $A_V(1)[0]$. It identifies $E_V(A_V)$ and $E_V(A_V(1))$, with their $B_V$-actions retained, with $(A_V\otimes_{A_V}B_V)[0]$ and $(A_V(1)\otimes_{A_V}B_V)[0]$. This uses flatness of the input over $A_V$, never flatness of $B$ over $A$.

On ordinary sheaves define $h^0_V(a\otimes b)=\varphi(a)b$ and $j^0_V(b)=1\otimes b$. The relation $(aa')\otimes b=a\otimes\varphi(a')b$ proves that $h^0_V$ is balanced; both maps are additive and $B_V$-linear. Their composites are the identity since $h^0_V(1\otimes b)=b$ and $1\otimes\varphi(a)b=a\otimes b$. These formulas commute with restriction, so the definition of sheaf tensor gives inverse sheaf maps. Localizing these degree-zero maps using step 1 defines the specified $\theta^0_V$.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), sheafification of the ordinary balanced tensor

proof.text: Define $h^1_V((z\otimes a)\otimes b)=z\otimes\varphi(a)b$ and $j^1_V(z\otimes b)=(z\otimes1)\otimes b$. These formulas are additive in the roots-module variable and in the coefficients. For $r\in\mathbf Z/N$, the inner balancing relation is respected because $z^r\otimes\varphi(a)b=z\otimes r\varphi(a)b$; outer $A$-balancing follows from $\varphi(aa')=\varphi(a)\varphi(a')$. For $j^1_V$, the relation $z^r\otimes b=z\otimes rb$ becomes $(z^r\otimes1)\otimes b=(z\otimes r1_A)\otimes b=(z\otimes1)\otimes r1_Bb$. The two composites on pure tensors are $z\otimes b$ and $(z\otimes1)\otimes\varphi(a)b=(z\otimes a)\otimes b$. Hence these are inverse $B_V$-linear sheaf maps after sheafification. By step 1 their degree-zero derived images give precisely $\theta^1_V$ and its asserted inverse.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product); explicit double balancing for the finite roots module

proof.text: Use the exact constant-coefficient inverse image and its constant-section ring identifications $c_R:f^{-1}R_T\cong R_{T'}$. Their coefficient square commutes: $c_B f^{-1}\varphi=\varphi c_A$, as both maps send a constant $a$ to $\varphi(a)$, and sheafification extends this equality. Regard coefficient extension and geometric pullback as ringed-topos pullbacks. The normalized derived composition comparisons identify their two composites, since their underlying geometric morphisms and structural ring maps agree. The monoidal-comparisons lemma computes these comparisons by ordinary pullback composition on flat-term K-flat complexes. The cochain-coherence lemma gives its scalar-association map $\kappa_K:u'^*(K\otimes_RR')\to(u^*K)\otimes_SS'$ explicitly. Specialize $R=A_T,R'=B_T,S=A_{T'},S'=B_{T'}$. For either degree-zero input $P$ of step 1, this says that $\lambda_P$ is the derived image of the $B_{T'}$-linear sheaf isomorphism $f_B^*(P\otimes_{A_T}B_T)\cong f_A^*P\otimes_{A_{T'}}B_{T'}$, sending the inverse image of a pure tensor $m\otimes b$ to $(f^{-1}m)\otimes c_B(f^{-1}b)$. The ringed tensor-pullback lemma ensures the pulled-back representatives are still flat-term K-flat, so both iterated computations are legitimate even for nonflat $B/A$. The same normalization identifies $e_R$ with $c_R$ in degree zero.

Write $z'$ for the image of an inverse-image root under $f^{-1}\mu_{N,T}\cong\mu_{N,T'}$. The twist-pullback lemma specifies $u_R$ by this root map, so $u_R(f^{-1}(z\otimes a))=z'\otimes c_R(f^{-1}a)$. On the inverse image of $((z\otimes a)\otimes b)$ the composite $\theta^1_{T'}E_{T'}(u_A)\lambda_{A_T(1)}$ therefore has value $z'\otimes\varphi(c_A(f^{-1}a))c_B(f^{-1}b)$. The other composite $u_B f_B^*(\theta^1_T)$ has value $z'\otimes c_B(f^{-1}(\varphi(a)b))$. These are equal by the coefficient-square equality and multiplicativity of $c_B$ in step 4. The comparison there is an isomorphism from the inverse-image sheafified tensor, so checking these generating pure tensors and their balanced relations suffices. Equality extends through sheafification. Both sides are the localizations of these actual equal degree-zero sheaf maps, giving the asserted equality in $D(T'_{\mathrm{et}},B)$, rather than just equality on cohomology.

source.place: Tag 03PK (section-kummer), roots-induced pullback identification; elementary coefficient-square calculation using step 4

proof.text: For the unit square the same calculation starts with the inverse image of $a\otimes b$. The composite $\theta^0_{T'}E_{T'}(e_A)\lambda_{A_T}$ sends it to $\varphi(c_A(f^{-1}a))c_B(f^{-1}b)$; the composite $e_Bf_B^*(\theta^0_T)$ sends it to $c_B(f^{-1}(\varphi(a)b))$. Step 4 identifies these expressions. They determine the same sheaf morphism by the balanced tensor construction, so their derived images are equal. This proves the unit equation with the specified canonical $e_A,e_B$, not with an arbitrarily chosen unit identification.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product); elementary unit calculation with the normalized comparisons of step 4

proof.text: The change-of-rings functor is exact and additive. For an integer $n$, use its canonical shift comparison to define $\theta^i_V[n]$ on $E_V(A_V(i)[n])$. On the representatives above, shifting places the single nonzero term in degree $-n$; all arrows in steps 2--6 are unchanged in that degree. Coefficient extension tensors with $B[0]$, so no interchange of two shifted factors and no extra sign occurs. The cochain scalar-association formula of step 4 has exactly these same components after shifting. Applying the localization functor to the equal shifted chain maps proves both equations after every common shift. For a finite family of shifted unit or twist summands $M_j$, additivity gives the canonical biproduct comparison $E_V(\bigoplus_jM_j)\cong\bigoplus_jE_V(M_j)$: its composites with inclusions are $E_V(\iota_j)$ and its components are $E_V(\pi_j)$. The identities $\pi_j\iota_k=\delta_{jk}$ and $\sum_j\iota_j\pi_j=1$ remain identities under an additive functor. Thus the direct sum of the specified shifted $\theta$ maps is the canonical comparison and preserves every summand inclusion and projection. The empty sum gives the zero-object comparison.
